newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines 1996 crude output down 75 pct vs 1995.
newsitem.headline: Philippines 1996 crude output down 75 pct vs 1995.

text.p: Philippine crude production is expected to fall by 75 percent to 270,000 barrels in 1996 from 1.067 million barrels last year, the Department of Energy said on Thursday.
In its yearend report, the energy department said that the sharp decline would be largely due to the stoppage of production at the West Linapacan wells in southwestern Philippines.
West Linapacan is the country's biggest oilfield with recoverable reserves of 100 million barrels but production ceased in January this year due to increasing water intrusion in the wells.
Total output from West Linapacan nosedived to 5,312 barrels this year from 703,011 barrels in 1995.

The two other fields, Nido and Matinloc also located in the in southwestern Philippines, were expected to produce a total of 269,017 barrels, 7.7 percent less than their 249,615 barrels combined output last year.
